canonical_topic: Temperature as the primary driver of short-term load variation
definition: Electricity demand rises in both cold winter conditions (heating) and hot summer conditions (air conditioning), making temperature the dominant explanator of day-to-day load swings.
core_idea: Because heating and cooling are major uses of electricity, load has a U-shaped (or similar) relationship with temperature, and short-term temperature forecasts are therefore central inputs to electrical demand forecasting.
key_points: As temperature falls in winter, electricity use for heating rises.
As temperature rises in summer, electricity use for air conditioning rises.
Temperature explains a large share of day-to-day variation in electricity demand.
This dependency is why short-term temperature forecasts are important to the power industry.
trading_implications: Traders and forecasters rely heavily on short-term temperature forecasts because temperature swings translate directly into demand (and price) swings.
